db_evidence.notes: The DB text tables (episodes, semantic_triples, topic_facts) around the 81570-81600s clue window describe the Jingubang acquisition narratively (protagonist 'holds and lifts long staff', location 水帘洞, dialogue) but never state the numeric player level at that exact moment -- the level number is only visible as an on-screen HUD/equipment digit, so it is retrievable only via clip_qa on the correct window. Between 79710s and 81584s the player leveled up from 93 to 94 (confirmed visually by rollouts 0 and 1 at 81584-81590s). root_causes: Wrong time window: the two 0-scored rollouts that did call clip_qa (03) or use retrieved text (04) anchored on level readings from BEFORE the acquisition moment (79680-79710s, level 93) rather than at the clue interval itself (81570-81600s, level 94), missing an intervening level-up.

Abandoning a correct retrieval hit: rollout 02 actually surfaced the correct visual_clips row (002719, 81570-81600) via semantic_search but did not act on it, instead chasing an unrelated later window (~84080-84420s) and ultimately giving up on a numeric answer.

Skipped visual verification: rollout 04 never invoked clip_qa at all and treated a DB text summary of an earlier (stale) equipment screen as if it applied at the acquisition moment, despite the visual-verification skill existing precisely for numeric on-screen values.

The numeric level is only reliably obtainable from the visual HUD at the exact clue interval; any window even ~2000s earlier gives a different, DB-supported but wrong answer, making this question sensitive to precise time-window selection.
what_worked: Rollouts 0 and 1 followed semantic_search hits (topic_facts/visual_clips) that pinpointed the 81570-81600s window matching the clue interval, then used clip_qa scoped tightly to that window with a question explicitly asking to distinguish player level from weapon stats, which the visual sub-agent answered correctly and consistently (94) across both.
transferable_lessons: For 'what level/stat when X happens' questions, always run clip_qa scoped to the exact clue/event interval, not to a nearby or 'shortly before' interval -- character level, stats, and other numeric state can change between text-table snapshots and the target moment.

When a semantic_search or run_sql hit already matches the narrative event described in the question (e.g. the exact acquisition dialogue/location), prioritize acting on that hit over exploring other, less on-topic candidate windows.

Do not substitute a DB text-table description of a numeric on-screen value for a live clip_qa check when the question depends on a precise number at a precise moment; text summaries can be stale relative to the exact time asked about.

If clip_qa reports 'no value visible' in one window, treat that as evidence the window is wrong and re-anchor to the retrieved clue interval, rather than falling back to a non-numeric answer (e.g. chapter name) as a substitute for the requested number.
